title: Five reactions, four equilibria
oneLine: An explicit mass-action realization reaches the positive-equilibrium bound, with a construction in every dimension.
abstract: This unrefereed candidate realizes the established Phillipson–Rojas polynomial chain as a quadratic mass-action network with n species, n+2 reactions, rank n and exactly n+1 positive nondegenerate equilibria for every integer n≥2. Integer products and positive rational rates attain the bound discussed by Banaji and Feliu. Two three-species examples provide an inflow-free realization with maximum product molecularity ten and an exact one-rate interval, and a reciprocal example with two sinks and two saddles. Quadratic restricts sources, not products; no experimental realization or global dynamical classification is claimed.

narration:
How many different steady states can a small reaction system support under the same rate constants?

This candidate gives a precise example: three chemical species, five reactions, and four distinct positive equilibria. Every equilibrium is nondegenerate, meaning that the local equilibrium equations have a nonsingular Jacobian. The count is supported by exact algebra, rather than a numerical plot alone.

The result extends to any number of species, starting with two. With two more reactions than species, the construction attains one more positive equilibrium than species. An earlier theorem supplied the matching upper bound.

The central contribution connects two mathematical settings. Phillipson and Rojas had already constructed a quadratic polynomial family with the maximum number of positive roots. This paper realizes that family using admissible mass-action reactions, integer product coefficients and positive rational rates. It does not claim a new abstract polynomial family.

One three-species example reduces to a curve crossing a horizontal line four times. In that example, two equilibria are locally attracting and two are saddles. Another example needs no inflow reaction and uses products containing at most ten molecules. Its four-equilibrium range is determined exactly as one rate changes.

Quadratic here limits the reactants to at most two molecules. Products may be larger. These are mathematical networks, not experimentally demonstrated chemistry, and the result does not promise four stable states or a global description of the dynamics.

The release includes the written proofs, reaction data, exact verification code and deliberately corrupted test cases. It remains an unrefereed candidate; internal checks and the supplied review do not establish authenticated external peer review.

This is Evidence Press, Five reactions, four equilibria, dated the fourth of October twenty twenty-six. The paper and evidence package are linked on the release page. This synthetic AI voice explains the research. It is not additional scientific evidence.

keyResults: For every integer n≥2, a quadratic (n,n+2,n) mass-action network attains exactly n+1 positive nondegenerate equilibria.
An explicit chemical realization of the existing Phillipson–Rojas extremal polynomial chain, with integer products and positive rational rates.
An inflow-free three-species, five-reaction example has maximum product molecularity ten and four positive nondegenerate equilibria precisely for 1568<L<117649/75 when its fourth rate is 1/L.
The reciprocal N=7, K=145 example has two locally attracting equilibria and two saddles, each with one unstable direction.
